conviction_note: No pre-release and no profit warning, so the quarter is new news on a thin name. On the confirmed report days the stock has moved a median 7.6% (8 prints, MFN/Yahoo), so abs_move is 7.0. p_up is only 55: the counterparties that reported Jul-Sep (Bergman & Beving in Sweden and Finland, Byggmax like-for-like +5.1%) lean mildly above ABG's 3% organic and 177m adj. EBITA bar, Norway is the known drag, and the bar comes from a single broker, so every finding is capped small. impact_sum (+1.5) exceeds the scaled +0.7 because the findings are small proxies that all lean one way, while p_up has to allow for the 50/50 sign history (4 up, 4 down).

findings.finding: Bergman & Beving, the closest Nordic counterparty, reported the same Jul-Sep quarter on 21 Oct. Its Finnish and Swedish companies saw increased construction and manufacturing activity and expect gradual improvement; Norwegian construction was wait-and-see after the autumn rate hike, and PPE demand was weak, especially in Norway. Sweden and Finland (most of Alligo's sales) lean above ABG's 3% organic; Norway is already assumed weak by ABG.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Organic growth and margin decide the day here: Q3'25 swung from -2.7% organic to a margin beat and rose 12.4%; Q2'26 had +30% adj. EBITA but organic slowed to 1.3% and it fell 2.5%; Q1'25 (weak market) fell 10.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Released two days before the print on a $150k/day name with three analysts. ABG's 3% organic estimate is dated 8 Oct, before it. Alligo is -0.2% since 20 Oct (125.0 to 124.8), so it shows no read-through rally; if the read-through were priced, the stock would have firmed on 21-22 Oct.
findings.independence: Byggmax Q3 like-for-like +5.1% (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b4806970d1c602f0d1d892d634fe84983&lang=en&src=listed). Net of Norway, which is about 45% of sales together with Finland and which ABG already models as subdued.

findings.finding: Byggmax Q3 2026: like-for-like sales +5.1%, net sales +7.1%, operating profit 292m (258) across Nordic building-materials stores. Q3 demand in Nordic building and DIY was better than flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: the organic-growth line has moved the stock 2.5-12% on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an adjacent-sector proxy (consumer and small-builder DIY, not B2B workwear and consumables), so it transmits weakly. It came out after ABG's bar was set.
findings.independence: Bergman & Beving Q2 (same quarter) reports higher Swedish and Finnish construction activity (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b69d5f724020f1d9844d71f50701e77fa&lang=en&src=listed)

findings.finding: Swedish manufacturing PMI was 58.1 in September and the Swedish building-material index rose 9.5% in Q2, its highest since Q1'22 (both cited in ABG's preview). The macro background to Swedish demand is firm.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: n/a: a macro series, not a company line.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the broker setting the bar already cites it, so it sits inside the 177m estimate and is sized near zero.

findings.finding: The bar was lowered on 8 Oct: ABG cut '26e adj. EBITA by 4%, mainly by cutting Sweden's margin from 9.7% to 9.2% after a change of analyst, not on new company data. The Q3 bar of 177m (7.5%) is only 0.3pp above the Q2 margin of 7.2%, in a seasonally stronger margin quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 at 7.2% adj. EBITA margin, +0.8pp, rose 12.4% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: A cut made for analyst-change reasons lowers the hurdle without new information on the business. The stock fell about 7% from 134 (23 Sep) to 124.8, so the expectation reset has, if anything, gone beyond the estimate cut.

findings.finding: The new CEO Samuel Alteborg (in post since 1 June) bought 7,500 B shares at SEK 135.50 on 2 Sep 2026, two months into the quarter being reported and about 8% above the current price.
findings.original_quote: Samuel Alteborg | Verkställande direktör (VD) | Förvärv | Alligo | Aktie | SE0009922305 | 2026-09-02 | 7 500 | Antal | 135,50 | SEK (CEO bought 7,500 shares at SEK 135.50)
findings.why_not_priced: It was public on 3 Sep but sits only in the FI insider register; no English wire or broker note picked it up. The stock has since fallen about 8%, so the market has not treated it as a signal. If it had been read, the stock would not be below the CEO's buy price two days before the print.

findings.finding: Norges Bank raised its policy rate 25bp to 4.50% on 23 Sep and said it was open to more, and Bergman & Beving reports Norwegian construction in wait-and-see after it. Tools Norway's outlook commentary is likely cautious.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Norway has been the persistent drag; Q2'25 ('market remains weak') opened -5.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: ABG already expects Norway to stay low but stable in H2. The residual is commentary risk from a new CEO in his first full-quarter report.

findings.finding: Ahlsell, Alligo's largest Nordic competitor, is selling off the inventory it acquired with Skydda's Nordic PPE business, per Bergman & Beving. That is possible price pressure in Nordic PPE and workwear, Alligo's own-brand and gross-margin category.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The gross-margin line moved +0.6pp (Q2'26) without lifting the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: An inference from a counterparty's remark about its own sales; no transmission to Alligo's pricing is documented, so it is sized small.
